summary: The 23 September listing is unusually rich in heavy-ion physics. The leading results are a carefully controlled quenched-lattice gradient-flow benchmark for the jet transport coefficient and a no-retuning open-quantum-system test of bottomonium suppression from Pb-Pb to O-O and Ne-Ne. Electromagnetic flow tomography and intermediate-energy pion transport provide useful model diagnostics, while the strongest transferable AI/ML work emphasizes calibrated surrogate uncertainty and posterior conditioning rather than headline accuracy.
strongest_paper: arXiv:2609.25089, Gradient Flow for the Jet Transport Coefficient: A Quenched Lattice Benchmark
top_takeaway: The gradient-flow lattice calculation is the day's cleanest methodological advance, while the bottomonium study gives the most direct near-term confrontation with new light-ion data.

papers.title: Gradient Flow for the Jet Transport Coefficient: A Quenched Lattice Benchmark
papers.abstract: The authors determine the leading-twist, nonperturbative medium contribution to the jet transport coefficient using gradient-flow energy-momentum tensors in quenched SU(3) lattice QCD over 0.76 Tc to 2.25 Tc. With three lattice spacings, controlled continuum and small-flow-time extrapolations, and one-loop short-distance matching, they obtain qhat/T^3 approximately 1.1 in the deconfined range and consistency with an earlier quenched calculation.

papers.title: System-size dependence of bottomonium suppression from Pb-Pb to light-ion collisions
papers.authors: Nora Brambilla; Tom Magorsch; Antonio Vairo
papers.abstract: Using the same NLO pNRQCD Lindblad evolution and microscopic transport coefficients previously constrained in Pb-Pb, the paper predicts integrated Upsilon double ratios in O-O and Ne-Ne hydrodynamic backgrounds. It reproduces the O-O sequential hierarchy within current uncertainties; Ne-Ne favors somewhat more suppression, but its uncertainty is still large.
papers.short_authors: Nora Brambilla; Tom Magorsch; Antonio Vairo

papers.title: Physical interpretation and limits of photon--dilepton radial-flow tomography
papers.abstract: A controlled expanding-fireball calculation shows why dilepton and flow-free photon inverse slopes track the same thermal scale, and that the photon shift probes an emission-weighted velocity component rather than a bulk radial-flow average. Prethermal source changes can create apparent flow, while multiple photon and dilepton windows help separate source composition from flow.

papers.title: Effects of in-medium NN inelastic cross sections and the high-momentum tail of nucleon momentum distributions on pion production in heavy-ion collisions
papers.authors: Pengcheng Li; A. B. Larionov; Yongjia Wang; Gaochan Yong; Qingfeng Li
papers.abstract: The authors add relativistic-BUU in-medium NN inelastic cross sections and a short-range-correlation high-momentum tail to UrQMD for intermediate-energy Au+Au collisions. The former suppresses NDelta production, the latter partly restores pion yield, and their combination improves comparisons with HADES pion yields and the FOPI charged-pion ratio.
papers.short_authors: Pengcheng Li; A. B. Larionov; Yongjia Wang; Gaochan Yong; Qingfeng Li

papers.title: Machine-learning modeling of nuclear collective observables and low-lying spectra
papers.authors: Dan Shi; Zu-Xing Yang; Xiao-Hua Fan; Zhi-Pan Li
papers.abstract: The Nuclear Collective Generator predicts a collective potential and six inertial functions on the beta-gamma plane from nuclear and shell descriptors, then propagates them through a five-dimensional collective Hamiltonian. Across 568 even-even nuclei it reports a 0.58 MeV mean RMS potential error and reasonable reproduction of deformation and low-lying spectroscopy.
papers.short_authors: Dan Shi; Zu-Xing Yang; Xiao-Hua Fan; Zhi-Pan Li

papers.title: Predictive Uncertainty for Neural CAE Surrogates
papers.authors: Kaustubh Tangsali; Mohammad Amin Nabian; Kelvin Lee; Carmelo Gonzales; Sanjay Choudhry
papers.abstract: The paper compares a Gaussian-process-based method, concrete Monte Carlo dropout, and deep ensembles for geometry-conditioned neural surrogates on three large aerodynamics and crash datasets. It evaluates error ranking, interval coverage, unfamiliar-input response, and derived quantities, finding that no method dominates across datasets or decision criteria.
papers.short_authors: Kaustubh Tangsali; Mohammad Amin Nabian; Kelvin Lee; Carmelo Gonzales; Sanjay Choudhry

papers.title: Variational objectives for amortized Bayesian inference in inverse problems: The role of posterior conditioning
papers.authors: Abhishek Srivastava; Arijit Hazra; Rajesh Dubbaku
papers.abstract: The authors analyze KL-, Jensen-Shannon-, and Jensen-Shannon-Wasserstein-regularized amortized inference with a full-covariance Gaussian encoder and physics surrogate. Analytic linear-Gaussian tests and nonlinear ODE/PDE inverse problems show that the preferred objective depends on posterior conditioning, with the Wasserstein variant improving strongly ill-conditioned cases.
papers.short_authors: Abhishek Srivastava; Arijit Hazra; Rajesh Dubbaku

cautions.title: Longitudinal Lambda Polarization as a Quantitative Constraint on Geometric Relaxation in Pb-Pb Collisions at 5.36 TeV
cautions.authors: Yilong Xie; Simin Wu; Laszlo P. Csernai
cautions.abstract: Across 48 initial states evolved with 3+1D ideal hydrodynamics and an isothermal local-equilibrium spin prescription, the authors fit a compact relation linking longitudinal Lambda polarization to freeze-out eccentricity and elliptic flow. A 12-state same-framework holdout retains roughly 86% explained variation, and a proof-of-principle inversion is applied to ALICE data.
cautions.short_authors: Yilong Xie; Simin Wu; Laszlo P. Csernai
